title: Ceva and Mobilint Bring Physical AI Closer to Everyday Devices
gist: Mobilint's REGULUS edge AI SoC, rated at 10 TOPS at under 3W, integrates Ceva's SensPro AI DSP and NeuPro-Nano NPU. It is the first production deployment of Ceva's NeuPro NPU family. REGULUS already powers Mobilint's MLD-R1 AI USB accelerator, which is now shipping, and targets robotics, machine vision, smart factories and similar physical-AI uses.

insights.claim: REGULUS pairs separate engines on one chip: Ceva's SensPro handles programmable sensing and signal processing, NeuPro-Nano runs always-on inference, and Mobilint's proprietary AI architecture sits alongside both. The aim is to match each stage of a physical-AI pipeline to the engine best suited to it.

themes.theme: Physical AI shifting inference to the edge

insights.claim: Devices that interact with the physical world, such as robots, drones, cameras and industrial equipment, increasingly need AI processing close to their sensors rather than in the cloud, so they can respond quickly within practical power and space limits.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: This supports the structural growth story for edge-AI silicon and IP vendors.

insights.claim: Mobilint targets smart factories, robotics, machine vision, security, medical devices and digital signage with REGULUS. It supports PyTorch, ONNX, Hugging Face, TensorFlow, TFLite and Keras to lower developers' switching costs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Compatibility with common frameworks is the main lever for adoption against other edge-AI chips.
